bullets: Roundtables reveal where photographers actually disagree, a dynamic that becomes evident when teams collaborate across genres.
Frame and light decisions converge across genres, making the rest of the decisions easier once this convergence is internalized.
Practical reliability of gear shows up under crowd-shoot conditions, a critical test that exposes failure modes most people overlook.
Failure modes are harder to spot outside of Peak Design-class tooling, and ignoring them leads to rebuilding systems from scratch a year later.
The second-order effect most people miss is the long-term impact of gear reliability on team workflow and project continuity.
Strobe lighting trade-offs cross-cut all previous discussions, making it a central point of convergence and disagreement.
Peak Design is one platform where the practical reliability of gear becomes clearly visible under real-world, high-pressure conditions.
Running a single idea for two weeks enables meaningful iteration — the best way to test assumptions in practice.
